title: [replay] feat(video-editor): make text labels editable and multi-line
body:
> **Replay of [niway-dev/kaipu-record#184](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/184)** for the code-review benchmark. Base `06388e6`, head `2c33d5b`: the same commits the original reviewers saw, so the diff is byte-identical. Never merged. Method and scoring: [wachiman/docs/benchmark](https://github.com/niway-dev/wachiman/tree/main/docs/benchmark). The original description follows.

---

## What was wrong

A text label in the video editor was **write-once and single-line**. Fixing a typo meant deleting the overlay and typing it again, which lost its timeline window, and there was no way to break a line at all.

The screenshot editor solved both a while ago. This ports that behaviour rather than inventing a second one.

## The part worth knowing

The line break had to be honoured in **three places, not one**, and missing any of them would have been worse than not shipping it. A break that survives editing, draws correctly in the preview, and then collapses in the exported video is discovered only after the export.

| Where | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Editing | `<input>`, single line, new labels only | `<textarea>`, reopens existing labels |
| Preview | one flat `<text>` | one `<tspan>` per line |
| Export SVG | one flat `<text>` | one `<tspan>` per line |

SVG `<text>` neither wraps nor honours a newline on its own, which is why both renderers needed it.

## Editing

Double-click reopens a label in place, prefilled, on the select tool only so it never collides with a drawing tool's click. Committing a reopened label replaces its text and keeps everything else — above all `start` and `end`, so retyping does not move when the label appears.

Plain Enter commits. Shift or Alt + Enter fall through to the textarea's own newline, the way a spreadsheet cell behaves. The box grows with its content so every line stays visible while typing.

## A bug found on the way

The selection rect was sized from `text.length` times a hand-copied `0.55`. A two-line label therefore drew an outline twice as wide as the text and only one line tall, so half of it was not selectable.

It now uses `textBoxPx`, which **already existed** in the screenshot editor's tools for exactly this and measures the longest line by the line count. `textLines`, `TEXT_LINE_HEIGHT` and `textBoxPx` are re-exported from that package, which `overlay-raster.ts` was already importing `TEXT_PX` and `HAND_FONT` from — so sharing is the established pattern here, not an exception.

## No migration

`text` is a plain string in the persisted scene and a newline is just data. Nothing to migrate.

## Tests

Each of the three surfaces fails silently on its own, so each is covered separately: the export SVG per line and its escaping, the shared box helper the preview now trusts, and the reopen-and-commit interaction — including that Shift+Enter does not commit and that the timeline window survives a retype.

The export fixture carries no `as VideoOverlay` cast, deliberately: the real type is what guards it, and it immediately caught two invented field names.

`bun run verify` green: 186 files, 1235 tests. The pre-push hook ran the full desktop E2E, also green.

## Out of scope, deliberately

Text size, colour, and the annotation inspector are untouched.

  - Edit existing text annotations by double-clicking them. Changes preserve the annotation’s timeline and other settings.

  - Multiline annotations now display with consistent line spacing and sizing in the editor and exported video.
